Uncertainty, precision, and retrospective revisions

Source: vignettes/uncertainty-and-revisions.Rmd
uncertainty-and-revisions.Rmd

UCDP data expose more than one form of uncertainty. Event records include spatial and temporal precision codes, while successive releases may revise previously published observations. ucdpR makes both dimensions inspectable without converting them into a single substantive uncertainty measure.

library(ucdpR)

events <- data.frame(
  id = 1:5,
  year = c(2020, 2020, 2021, 2021, 2021),
  where_prec = c(1, 2, 3, 6, NA),
  date_prec = c(1, 2, 4, 5, 1),
  best = c(4, 8, 2, 12, 1)
)

Precision as reported uncertainty

Begin by showing the distribution rather than immediately discarding less precise observations.

ucdp_precision(events)
#> # A tibble: 9 × 6
#>   dimension variable    code label                                       n share
#>   <chr>     <chr>      <int> <chr>                                   <int> <dbl>
#> 1 spatial   where_prec     1 Exact location                              1   0.2
#> 2 spatial   where_prec     2 Within approximately 25 km                  1   0.2
#> 3 spatial   where_prec     3 Second-order administrative division        1   0.2
#> 4 spatial   where_prec     6 Country only                                1   0.2
#> 5 spatial   where_prec    NA Missing                                     1   0.2
#> 6 temporal  date_prec      1 Exact date                                  2   0.4
#> 7 temporal  date_prec      2 Two-to-six-day range                        1   0.2
#> 8 temporal  date_prec      4 Eight-to-thirty-day range or month kno…     1   0.2
#> 9 temporal  date_prec      5 More than one month but less than one …     1   0.2
ucdp_precision(events, by = "year")
#> # A tibble: 10 × 7
#>     year dimension variable    code label                                n share
#>    <dbl> <chr>     <chr>      <int> <chr>                            <int> <dbl>
#>  1  2020 spatial   where_prec     1 Exact location                       1 0.5  
#>  2  2020 spatial   where_prec     2 Within approximately 25 km           1 0.5  
#>  3  2021 spatial   where_prec     3 Second-order administrative div…     1 0.333
#>  4  2021 spatial   where_prec     6 Country only                         1 0.333
#>  5  2021 spatial   where_prec    NA Missing                              1 0.333
#>  6  2020 temporal  date_prec      1 Exact date                           1 0.5  
#>  7  2020 temporal  date_prec      2 Two-to-six-day range                 1 0.5  
#>  8  2021 temporal  date_prec      1 Exact date                           1 0.333
#>  9  2021 temporal  date_prec      4 Eight-to-thirty-day range or mo…     1 0.333
#> 10  2021 temporal  date_prec      5 More than one month but less th…     1 0.333

An analysis can then define transparent thresholds and compare results across them.

strict_sample <- ucdp_filter_precision(
  events, where_prec = 1, date_prec = 1:2
)

broader_sample <- ucdp_filter_precision(
  events, where_prec = 1:3, date_prec = 1:4
)

nrow(strict_sample)
#> [1] 1
nrow(broader_sample)
#> [1] 3

Revisions between releases

The comparison function accepts preloaded data frames, which makes the core operation reproducible and easy to demonstrate without downloading data.

old <- data.frame(
  id = 1:4,
  year = c(2020, 2020, 2021, 2021),
  best = c(4, 8, 2, 12),
  where_prec = c(1, 2, 3, 6),
  version = "24.1"
)

new <- data.frame(
  id = 2:5,
  year = c(2020, 2021, 2021, 2021),
  best = c(8, 3, 12, 1),
  where_prec = c(2, 2, 6, 1),
  version = "25.1"
)

comparison <- ucdp_compare_versions(
  "ged",
  old_version = "24.1",
  new_version = "25.1",
  key = "id",
  old_data = old,
  new_data = new
)

comparison$overview
#> # A tibble: 1 × 7
#>   old_rows new_rows matched added removed modified unchanged
#>      <int>    <int>   <int> <int>   <int>    <int>     <int>
#> 1        4        4       3     1       1        1         2
comparison$variables
#> # A tibble: 3 × 2
#>   variable   n_changed
#>   <chr>          <int>
#> 1 best               1
#> 2 where_prec         1
#> 3 year               0
comparison$added
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>      id  year  best where_prec version
#>   <int> <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1     5  2021     1          1 25.1
comparison$removed
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>      id  year  best where_prec version
#>   <int> <dbl> <dbl>      <dbl> <chr>  
#> 1     1  2020     4          1 24.1
comparison$modified
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>      id changed_columns 
#>   <int> <chr>           
#> 1     3 best, where_prec

Cell-level output is useful when the direction and magnitude of individual changes matter.

cell_comparison <- ucdp_compare_versions(
  "ged", "24.1", "25.1",
  key = "id", old_data = old, new_data = new,
  detail = "cells"
)
cell_comparison$cell_changes
#> # A tibble: 2 × 4
#>      id variable   old_value new_value
#>   <int> <chr>      <chr>     <chr>    
#> 1     3 best       2         3        
#> 2     3 where_prec 3         2

For official releases, omit old_data and new_data and supply exact version identifiers:

official_comparison <- ucdp_compare_versions(
  "ged", old_version = "24.1", new_version = "25.1"
)

Revision frequency is not automatically measurement error: changes may reflect new information, corrected coding, altered definitions, or expanded coverage. The comparison identifies what changed; substantive interpretation still requires the relevant codebooks and version histories.

Direct integration with uncertainUCDP will be documented after its current API and the meaning of the exchanged objects have been verified. Until then, the outputs remain ordinary tibbles that can be inspected or transformed by downstream uncertainty workflows without an undocumented dependency.
